Walkways and Steps

Plan the route before choosing the pattern.

The path should connect the places you need to reach and fit the slope and access of the yard. We can discuss its route, curves, landings, step locations, borders, and how it meets nearby patios or concrete. Lighting-ready details can also be considered when they are part of the plan.

  • Front entries, side yards, and garden paths
  • Steps, landings, and changes in grade
  • Curves, borders, and paver patterns
  • Connections to patios, driveways, and existing surfaces

A Few Things to Think Through

A good path begins with where it needs to go.

An entry path, side-yard walkway, or set of garden steps should suit the route people actually take. The turns, slope, landing areas, and connections to doors and paved spaces all help determine the final layout.

01

Route and width

Identify the start and destination, how the path will be used, and where it needs to pass existing trees, beds, or utilities.

02

Slope and steps

Changes in elevation, landings, and the available run affect how a walkway or stair connection can be laid out.

03

Finishing the connections

Borders and transitions at a driveway, patio, porch, or lawn help the route feel connected to the property.

How the Work Comes Together

The steps for this project.

01

02

03

Questions About Walkways and Steps

A few useful things to know.

Every property is different. These answers can help you prepare for a conversation about the site and the work.

Can a walkway be built on a sloped yard?

A sloped site can be reviewed to see how the route, grade, steps, and landings should work together. The possible layout depends on the space and the amount of elevation change.

Can steps and a walkway be part of the same project?

Yes. They can be planned as one continuous route, including where steps begin, where a landing may help, and how the path meets the home or another paved area.

Can a new walkway match my patio?

The team can discuss paver colors, patterns, and borders that coordinate with an existing patio. Matching depends on the original material and what is currently available.
